## How to read the memory block
The "slots" field is a list of slot subgraphs. Each slot has:
  - "slot" and "slot_label": canonical English slot key (e.g. FAMILY).
  - "messages": edges in that slot. Each edge has:
      • subject, relation, object — nodes and relation type;
      • created_at_datetime — when the fact was added to the graph;
      • ttl — fact lifetime ("inf" = permanent).

## Rules for using memory
  1. Rely on graph facts when they are relevant to the question.
  2. Follow links across slots — the answer may require combining several subgraphs.
  3. When several slots contribute different details — structure the answer by topic.
  4. If two facts conflict — the newer one (later created_at_datetime) wins.
  5. If memory is empty or irrelevant — answer from general knowledge.
  6. In your answer, do not mention slots, memory, or how memory works; do not invent facts about the user.
